ai.title: Add terminal command analytics tracking
ai.summary: Added AnalyticsEvent.TERMINAL_COMMAND_COMPLETED to common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts. runTerminalCommand in npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts now calls trackEvent with command, result, stdout, exitCode, mode, and processType on completion. resolveCommand signature updated to include exitCode across runBackgroundCommand and runCommandPty.

eli5.text: When you run a command in the terminal through the assistant, the system now quietly records details about that command, including what you typed, whether it succeeded or failed, and any error codes returned. This tracking applies to commands run in the background as well as interactive ones, so failed terminal commands can now be identified and investigated. The data is sent to the product team's analytics, helping them understand which terminal actions break or behave unexpectedly.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.257
ai.summary: Package version incremented to 1.0.257 in npm-app/package.json. Reverts to 1.0.255 baseline. Affects npm-app package metadata.

eli5.text: Your copy of the assistant was quietly updated to version 1.0.257, which bundles together the improvements made since the last major baseline. If you reinstall or get the latest update, you'll pick up fixes like cleaner tool displays, better handling of terminal output, and new setup guidance for Windows computers. There's nothing you have to do right now, existing installs keep working, but the next time you update, these changes will be ready.

ai.title: Add hasGit property to analytics identify calls
ai.summary: Extracted `gitCommandIsAvailable` from `npm-app/src/checkpoints/file-manager.ts` to new shared utility `npm-app/src/utils/git.ts`. Updated `npm-app/src/client.ts` to include `hasGit` boolean in analytics `identify` calls. This enables tracking of native git availability across user sessions.

eli5.text: The assistant now silently checks whether git (a tool for tracking code changes) is installed on your computer and reports that fact back to the developers. You won't see anything different, but the developers gain a small piece of information about how often git is available across user setups. The check itself was already working; this change simply makes that information visible in analytics.

ai.title: Add cd analytics tracking
ai.summary: Added CHANGE_DIRECTORY analytics event tracking in npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts. The event fires during `cd` execution in runCommandPty, capturing source path, destination, and whether the target is a subdirectory. This provides visibility into directory navigation patterns within the CLI.

eli5.text: When you change directories in the command line, the program now records which folder you came from, which folder you went to, and whether that new folder is inside your current project. This only affects people using the command-line tool, and you won't see any visible difference in how it works today. The tracking data is used internally to understand how people navigate between folders.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.258
ai.summary: Incremented version to 1.0.258 in npm-app/package.json. Added trailing newline to package.json. Internal release metadata update.

eli5.text: This update bumps the assistant's version number and adds a few behind-the-scenes tracking features, like noting whether Git is available on your system and recording when you switch directories in the terminal. It also refines how some internal data is formatted. These changes are mostly invisible to you as a user - you won't see new buttons or features - but they help the team understand how people use the assistant. The update went live today and applies to anyone using the latest version of the assistant.

ai.title: Refine schema stringification formatting
ai.summary: Updated `stringifySchema` to generate JSON-like output with comments for descriptions and defaults, replacing the previous text-based format. Imports adjusted in `backend/src/system-prompt/prompts.ts` and `web/src/components/docs/mdx/schema-display.tsx` to use `common/src/json-config` paths and remove the unused schema name argument. `common/src/json-config/stringify-schema.ts` now handles indentation, optional types, and default values explicitly. Minor description text tweaks in `common/src/json-config/constants.ts`.

eli5.text: If you open the configuration documentation today, the technical reference for the project settings file now reads like a structured, annotated outline instead of plain prose, with each option shown in a JSON-style layout and helpful notes about what it does and its default value. The underlying engine that builds this reference switched to a format that prints the settings in tidy, indented blocks and includes descriptions and default values inline. This affects anyone reading the built-in documentation for the configuration file, which is now rendered as formatted JSON rather than generic text.

ai.title: Split bigquery into @codebuff/bigquery package
ai.summary: BigQuery client and schema moved from common/src/bigquery to packages/bigquery, exported as @codebuff/bigquery. Backend and scripts now import from the new package instead of deep paths into common. The new package depends on common and @google-cloud/bigquery.

eli5.text: You probably won't notice anything directly, but behind the scenes the team reorganized how the app talks to Google's BigQuery storage. Instead of parts of the code digging through a messy shared folder to find BigQuery tools, they created one clean, clearly labeled package that everything now pulls from. This is housekeeping that makes the system easier to maintain and less likely to break when they need to update those tools later.

ai.title: CLI decouples working directory from project root
ai.summary: CLI and backend logic now separate `workingDirectory` from `projectRoot`. `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` adds `setWorkingDirectory`/`getWorkingDirectory`, while `npm-app/src/cli.ts` updates prompt rendering and path resolution to use the active working directory. Tool handlers in `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts` drop the explicit `projectPath` argument, relying on `getProjectRoot()` internally, and `backend/src/tools.ts` clarifies that agent operations remain anchored to the project root regardless of user `cd` commands.

eli5.text: When you navigate to a different folder inside your project while using the assistant, the command-line tools you see (like tab completion or the prompt) now correctly look at your current folder instead of the main project folder. This only affects what you see at the prompt, the assistant itself still reads and writes files relative to your main project folder, so your actual code changes remain anchored to the project root regardless of where you navigated. This behavior is already live.

ai.title: bigquery and billing build use tsc --build
ai.summary: packages/bigquery/package.json and packages/billing/package.json switch build script from tsc to tsc --build. tsconfig.base.json adds declaration and declarationMap true. Fixes bigquery package deployment.

eli5.text: When the system packages the internal tools for BigQuery and Billing so they can be shipped to customers, those tools now compile their helper files correctly and include the right type information. Previously the build step used a simpler compiler mode that skipped generating some of the files other tools rely on, which caused the BigQuery package to fail to deploy. The fix switches that build step to a more complete compiler mode and tells the shared configuration to produce both the finished code and its accompanying description files, so the package deploys successfully now.

ai.title: cd command handles outside-root path and non-directory targets
ai.summary: handleChangeDirectory in npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts now returns true for outside-root paths and validates directory existence via isDir before executing cd. Out-of-root errors print a 3-step manual restart guide. Non-directory targets return false without setting working directory.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to switch to a different folder, it now handles two messy situations more gracefully. If you try to go to a folder outside your current project, instead of silently failing it tells you to exit, change directory manually, and restart; the command is now treated as handled rather than a hard error. If you try to switch to something that isn't a folder at all, it quietly refuses instead of crashing or leaving you in the wrong place. You'd notice this if you tried to point the tool at a wrong or out-of-reach location.

ai.title: Add Nx build system and bigquery path alias
ai.summary: Introduced Nx (^20.8.1) with nx.json configuring build/typecheck caching and dependency graphs. Added @codebuff/bigquery path alias and project reference to backend/tsconfig.json. Updated .gitignore to exclude .nx/cache and .nx/workspace-data. Scope limited to repo tooling and backend TypeScript configuration.

eli5.text: Your computer now remembers the results of repetitive tasks like building or checking your code, so the next time it needs to do the same work, it can skip straight to the finish instead of starting over. This means tasks that used to take minutes might now finish in seconds, especially when nothing has actually changed since the last run. The system also now treats a section of code called BigQuery like a first-class part of the project, so any code that depends on it can be checked and built independently. You wouldn't see a new feature or button, but behind the scenes your development tools are faster and more organized.

ai.title: Add clean script to package.json
ai.summary: Added `clean` script to `package.json`. Runs `bun run --filter` across `common`, `./packages/**`, `backend`, `codebuff`, and `web` to execute their respective `clean` tasks. Affects repo-level tooling only.

eli5.text: A single line was added that lets the codebase reset its own build files. Running one command now clears out temporary build output from the common library, the packages folder, the backend service, codebuff, and the web app all at once. This affects only the developer workflow. It's available today.

ai.title: Fix Windows command echo handling
ai.summary: Simplified echo line counting in `runCommandPty` for Windows (`win32`) to a fixed value of 1. Added logic to detect command completion by checking if `promptIdentifier` appears in the processed buffer, ensuring proper termination regardless of echo state.

eli5.text: When you run a command on a Windows machine, the software sometimes got confused about when the command was actually done because Windows echoes your typed text back on screen, and the old counting method was overly complicated and could miscount. The tool now uses a simpler, fixed counting approach for Windows and instead waits to see your usual command prompt reappear in the output as the clear signal that the command finished. This affects anyone using the internal assistant on Windows who runs terminal commands. You would notice commands on Windows ending more reliably without hanging, though you wouldn't see any visible change to the command output itself.

ai.title: Version bump 1.0.259
ai.summary: Version bump 1.0.259. Increment in `npm-app/package.json`. No functional changes.

eli5.text: If you're running the assistant, updating to this version installs a batch of smaller behind-the-scenes improvements that shipped this week, rather than any single new feature you'd see right away. The update itself just bumps the version number used to publish those bundled changes, so your install stays current with the latest fixes and refinements.
